text_fidelity_a:
TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps The TP-Link Powerline Adapter is a great kit for spanning distances or to help boost the signal of a router in the home. What this does is take the signal from your modem or router and transmits it over your power lines, and this allows you to have signal where you might otherwise have environmental issues blocking a wireless signal such as concrete, steel beams or just distance. One of the major drawbacks to this product is that the plugs you are using must be on the same circuit, though most people shouldn't run into this issue.

One of the biggest issues I have with this product is the fact that it isn't plug and play, not by the true definition. You HAVE to run the software to get your computer to recognize the plugs. I attempted to use them without running the software first and my computer couldn't connect to my home network. After running the software, it connected no problem. So Please take note: THIS IS NOT TRUE PLUG AND PLAY.

These are Gigabit (please note "Gigabit" is not the same as "Gigabyte") adapters and work very well. I was able to watch Youtube.com and Hulu without any issues. The web pages loaded as quickly as if I were directly connected to my router or on my wifi network.

Pros:

-Great for Larger houses to get a better signal for the home network.
-Good for streaming and downloads.
-Creates a good enough connection to act as if you are directly connected to the modem/router.

Cons:

-MUST be on the same circuit!
-Can't use a surge strip or UPS(uninterruptable power source) with these adapters so there is a risk of electrical shock to your computer during a storm.
-NOT TRUE Plug and Play. YOU MUST RUN THE SOFTWARE FIRST.

3.5 stars
text_fidelity_b: TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps

While this isn't meant to be babyproof, I've found that the cage-like design and locking mechanism not only keep my cords tidier, but also makes them a lot less obvious and exciting to baby so that when it is placed out of reach, he isn't always clamoring to be lifted up to it, as he does with high-up cords that are not as hidden.

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. So stiff that in fact I doubted whether I was really supposed to slide them out and was afraid I'd break the thing. I also found the locking/ opening/ closing mechanism too stiff - in fact, I gashed my finger when it opened unexpectedly after having to push it harder than I should have to open it.

The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all.

I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black

StarTech.com 4-Port USB 3.0 SuperSpeed Hub - Portable Mini Multiport USB Travel Dock - USB Extender Black for Business PC/Mac, laptops (ST4300MINU3B) This is an excellent 4-port USB3 hub. I tested it with a couple of USB3 flash drives (sticks), and saw data transfers (from/to main SSD drive) in both directions to the limit of the drives (60-90 MB/s). I also tested with an external USB3 SSD drive, and saw transfers to the limit of that drive (150 MB/s write, 350MB/s read). Needless to say, I used good USB3 cables to connect.

I also tested charging my phone with the hub. This worked, but I did get a notification on the phone that it was charging slower than normal. I don't find this surprising, I think you'd charge directly from an outlet or from your computer, you wouldn't use the hub unless you really needed to do so. So ok for an emergency bit of charging.

I've used other StarTech hubs (and various other products), and have not been disappointed. If you need a solid USB3 hub, this one deserves consideration. But I always do price comparisons, since there are competitive products that are sometimes cheaper.

text_fidelity_a:
Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 50 Ft White Flat 40Gbps High Speed Shielded RJ45 LAN Cable I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.
text_fidelity_b: Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 50 Ft White Flat 40Gbps High Speed Shielded RJ45 LAN Cable

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

text_fidelity_a:
Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27 We can not find the remote for our Roku or downstairs TV which is a Samsung since we had to remodel over a long period of time due to a flood which started it all. I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.
text_fidelity_b: Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27

So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.

text_fidelity_a:
Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner EDIT: added pictures.

Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!).

I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know!

It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice.

The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced.

Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows.

There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here:

Directions say:
-- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?)

--Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces

--Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it

--Ingredients:
Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin.

--Made in China
text_fidelity_b: Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner

text_fidelity_a:
ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.
text_fidelity_b: ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Wireless Bluetooth In Ear Headphones: Noise Cancelling Sports Workout Ear Buds for Exercise and Running - Cordless, Sweatproof Sport Earphones, Built-In Microphone, EXTRA BASS –Black WF-SP700N/B I use active noise canceling (ANC) headphones all the time and prefer them to normal headphones as I tend to work in noisy environments and I’ve found that with ANC engaged I can play music at lower volumes. I like Sony headphones so I was excited to try these ANC ear buds. They’re a bit unusual in a few ways but they work well and are worth their asking price.

These are truly wireless and have no physical connection between them. Power them both on and they find one another. They pair via Bluetooth to a phone, tablet or PC, and the connection is stable up to about 40’ around corners. This is a good start.

There are several modes to these when it comes to the ANC function and each has its uses. I usually just use full ANC without any of the ambient sound modes turned on as it gives the best music experience. One of the two ambient modes is optimized for speech and voice, the other for more generalized noise. Neither completely cut off noise canceling, but rather they allow different bands of outside noise to come through. In full ANC mode, these are good noise cancellers, though not as aggressive as some others like Bose.

These have proven to be comfortable, and they have the little wings on each bud for keeping them in place in your ear. I used them while working in the yard and never once did I have a problem with slipping or falling out, even though I have the wrong size silicone insert on one of them.

The sound is very good but I would stop short of calling it outstanding. The bass is heavier than I like though not so bad that it gives me a headache unless I pump the volume up too much. The midrange is warm and full, and the highs are bright and crisp without being piercing. The sound can be adjusted a bit in the app that you can download, as it has an equalizer of sorts that lets you tweak the levels or choose a preset.

Ah, the app… This is the primary downside of these. The method to adjust these is either an Android or iOS app, not a physical piece of hardware and there is no Windows equivalent (for those who want to use these with a PC). The app is a little clunky though fairly self-explanatory and it does do what it’s supposed to do. Given a choice between an app or an additional piece of hardware, I would choose the hardware.

These charge up in the carrying case, which has leads that connect to each bud. Pay attention when you put these in the case – it is possible to reverse them, and while it hurts nothing the charging doesn’t work well… The case has some sort of battery in it and it charges the buds without being plugged in itself, though it does require occasional charging. Charging is fast – I charged them from empty to full in about an hour. One thing that could be improved, though: the buds can be popped in the charger while still powered on, and the act of charging them does not make them cut off. So, you can end up with dead buds and a dead charger too.

These are decent wireless sport buds that have good sound and good ANC functions. They’re comfortable and not overpriced. There are a couple of areas for improvement, particularly in charging but also in the app control, that would make these even better.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Wireless Bluetooth In Ear Headphones: Noise Cancelling Sports Workout Ear Buds for Exercise and Running - Cordless, Sweatproof Sport Earphones, Built-In Microphone, EXTRA BASS –Black WF-SP700N/B

text_fidelity_a:
Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White We've been using an older first generation Portal and like it very much. I was not expecting to be so impressed with this one, but wow have they managed to improve almost everything about the original! It still has the very cool zoom-and-pan style camera feature that follows the subject, as well as all the fun filters and of course my kids' favorite, story time... but the polish and style of this unit is really premium. The speaker is fantastic and LOUD if you want it to be. The clarity and bass rivals my bookshelf speakers so well, sometimes the kids play music off it and I could have sworn they were using the speakers in the living room. But the biggest improvement over the previous generation is the ability to run off battery power and move around. The "portable portal" honestly makes so much sense, I wonder why the original stationary style ones came out first!
Make no mistake, it is NOT a tablet, it is not thin and won't fit in an attaché case nicely. It is wedge-shaped making it stand easily at an ideal angle, and even has a cut-out handle to pick it up and carry it to a better location for video chat. This is great for bringing it to wherever my kids happen to be congregating currently, and it can be put back up on the shelf when done to charge. Like the original Portals, it has Alexa built in and can act as an Echo for most things, however it is very tied into Facebook's ecosystem. That means that although it seems to run something akin to Android behind the scenes, this is NOT going to offer a standard App store, and even things like Youtube are not available for it (licensing issues with Google I'd suppose). However there is a browser, and you can navigate to YouTube and play it from the website just fine, although a proper app would be much easier to navigate. It does have Plex support, which I found interesting since I have a Plex server. I never thought I'd find Plex available where Youtube is not! Meanwhile, between Youtube in the browser, Amazon Music through Alexa and content on Plex, there are plenty of ways to make it a music streamer on that glorious better-than-it-should-sound speaker. And the camera works just as well if not better than the OG Portal!
Calls over FB Messenger or Whatsapp work well, and of course the camera / mic not only have a switch to toggle, but the camera has a physical cover that can slide over the lens in case you don't trust Facebook not to snoop. But that's another story.
All things considered, this is a solid product.
text_fidelity_b: Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White

text_fidelity_a:
Medialink Wireless Router - Renewed (150 Mbps) - Easy YouTube Setup Video (Part# MWNWAPR150N) I purchased this router to create a small two-computer network in my apartment. My PC is a refurbished and souped up Gateway running Windows Vista, and I bought an older Toshiba laptop, also refurbished and running Windows XP Home Edition. I wanted to be able to sit in my living room or on the patio while working once in awhile, rather than being chained to my home office PC. No gaming consoles, DVRs, or other components to connect.

The setup literature and accompanying CD shipped with the router are invaluable, easy to understand, even for a non-techie like me. However, don't expect your setup to proceed with no glitches! You may have to reset your cable modem two or three times, or restart the various components two or three times. Take your time, follow directions, keep your wits about you, and think about possible causes and likely solutions and you should have no trouble setting up this router.

The day after my order, I also received a lengthy, substantive email from Mediabridge Products, thanking me for my order and supplying me with all kinds of background, links, and telephone technical support information, so I felt confident that I had resources handy during the setup if necessary. So far the router is working like a charm. I recommend it, especially if you're interested in a fairly simple LAN setup!

text_fidelity_a:
Winegard FL5500A FlatWave Amped Digital HD Indoor Amplified TV Antenna (4K Ready / ATSC 3.0 Ready / High-VHF / UHF), 60 Mile Long Range, Black/White, 6 Feet Got this on Amazon Lightning Deal for $50 but it's just not worth that much, IMO, so I'll be returning it. I do live on the bottom floor of a 3-story apartment building that's built into a hill (so 2 stories on the other side), with a patch of pine trees in front of me, so I fully understand that there are many hurdles for my particular set up. However, I also live in a major city, not 30 miles from all the broadcast towers, and while this antenna can pick up those channels, it's incredibly inconsistent at holding the signal. Pictures do a slight pixelation maybe every five minutes or so; nothing major, but enough to be annoying, and so I don't think this particular antenna is worth fifty bucks - I feel like I could get that same level of "service" from a cheap-y model. I also am using the amplifier.

As far as decor - it's non-obtrusive, and has a long cable so finding good placement for best reception is pretty easy.

My mom snagged one of the Amazon-version ones for $25 a few hours later in the Lightning Deals. I could see paying $25 for this, simply because it's less gaudy than rabbit ears, but not because I believe you're getting anything more reception-wise.
text_fidelity_b: Winegard FL5500A FlatWave Amped Digital HD Indoor Amplified TV Antenna (4K Ready / ATSC 3.0 Ready / High-VHF / UHF), 60 Mile Long Range, Black/White, 6 Feet

text_fidelity_a: ASUS C200 Chromebook 11.6 Inch (Intel Celeron, 2 GB, 16GB SSD, Black/Silver) I have an aging netbook that isn't really worth turning on anymore, and wanted a portable solution with a keyboard.  Unfortunately, the netbook market kinda died, but then again, the Chromebooks have seem to come into their own.  As a fan of ASUS's products, I couldn't turn this little guy down, especially at this price.  Over all, the build quality feels solid.  It's obviously plastic, but the construction is solid.  The screen on this Chromebook is serviceable, but has limited viewing angles.  Netflix and Amazon Prime videos seem to stream just fine.  The biggest surprise for me is the keyboard and touch pad.  Normally I have a hard time with touch pads, but this one is great!  And the keyboard feels like it belongs on a computer that cost 3 or 4 times as much (I own a $1000 ASUS gaming laptop.)  When it comes to performance, I do question how long this will last...  Scrolling though webpages isn't as smooth as it would be on a decent laptop, and I know that the guts of this machine aren't meant for high performance.  Regardless, this is definitely worth purchasing for convenience and portability!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS C200 Chromebook 11.6 Inch (Intel Celeron, 2 GB, 16GB SSD, Black/Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
VELCRO Brand ONE-WRAP Cable Ties, 100Pk, 8 x 1/2" Black Cord Organization Straps, Thin Pre-Cut Design, Wire Management for Organizing Home, Office and Data Centers I use these exclusively for cable management - I pass the end of the strap through the slot so that the strap is permanently secured to the cable, then bundle the cord up. EZPZ. Great value for the money, I bought two bags to organize my cables and I should probably be set for the next twenty years or so. Much better than constantly scavenging velcro straps from new purchases. I prefer these to wire ties, as they can be secured to the cable, stick better, apply force over a broader area and look a far bit more orderly when properly installed.

The straps are of good quality, adhere very well, and are easy to remove when you want to. The length is suited for wrapping up, say, most of your average 10-15ft computer or AV cables, it hasn't been a problem yet.

Only annoying thing is that when the factory punched out the slots in the strap, it only did so partially, so the little central bit is still stuck to the velcro most of the time. Bothersome, but not excessive so, you just have to tear it off each time. Another nitpick would be that I prefer my straps to have a constant width, rather than tapering down near the end - again, looks neater IHMO.

Other than that, would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: VELCRO Brand ONE-WRAP Cable Ties, 100Pk, 8 x 1/2" Black Cord Organization Straps, Thin Pre-Cut Design, Wire Management for Organizing Home, Office and Data Centers

The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2)

ClearStream Micron-R Indoor HDTV Antenna with Reflector - 35 Mile Range I have a roof-top antenna that worked well for analog stations but, when I converted to digital, I went from receiving 8 stations to just 1. After trying a few other antennas, I came across the ClearStream 4. I'm able to pull in 20+ digital stations perfectly, and 4 more so-so. Several analog stations come in as well, but the picture is not nearly as good as the digitial stations.

The antenna is well-made, but is a bit of a pain to assemble - lots of pieces to screw together. It only takes about 10 minutes, but you'll probably need to utter a few choice words since it's hard to get the screws to line up properly. The directions are pretty spotty, but give you the essential information. The brackets are heavy-duty, and everything is either aluminum or plastic, so it should hold up well to the elements if I put it outside. Right now, it is in my attic, and may stay there since it pulls in all the stations I want to watch. It does not come with a cable.

It's pretty compact given its performance, and much more compact that the DB8 (another Antenna Direct model with about the same specifications). Very happy with the performance. Also have a DB2 -- see my comments on that review that compare it to this antenna in terms of performance.

text_fidelity_a:
turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus I'm really impressed with this bluetooth receiver. Unlike another brand I tried, this offers outstanding sound quality, which is my main reason for using it.

It's very straightforward to set up. Just plug in the receiver (it's very small - less bulky than most "wall warts" that are present on power plugs), pair it with your bluetooth source, and plug the included cables into a stereo.

I'm using this with a Kindle Fire 8.9. Pairing was quick and simple.

The connection to the stereo can be done via a single cable or using a two cable (L/R) setup. Cables for both options are included. I'm using the L/R option, and plugged the cables into the TAPE input on my stereo receiver.

The sound quality is excellent. It is very hard to tell the difference in quality when streaming audio via this receiver versus playing a CD on the receiver. Movie dialog was outstanding as well.

The fact that it does not require a battery is a plus and a minus. On the plus side, no need to worry about recharging or swapping batteries. On the down side, it was a bit of a problem for me to get the cables routed since the wall outlet near my stereo is not easily accessible. I wound up running a short extension cord so that I could plug in the receiver close enough to the stereo so that the L/R cables would reach.

As a bonus, it includes a USB port so you can use it to recharge your phone/tablet/etc.

That one minor issue aside, I'm very impressed with the performance of this product. Highly recommend.

It worked pretty well and got quite a few channels.  This one, however, works better and a few more channels come in clearly and consistently.  I tried it too without the USB power and it still works well, but without the power, not all the channels came in.  For the little extra that this costs over cheaper antennas, it is worth it. The only thing I can see wrong with this is that since it is powered, it does use some electricity, whereas cheaper antennas don't. If you don't use the TV every day, unplug the power.  If you have pets that tend to chew things, watch out for them with the long cords on this.  Very satisfied with it and may get another one for other televisions in the house, once we cut off cable, which we are doing soon.  You recover your cost of the device with just one month of cable. text_fidelity_a:
ASIMOM Bluetooth Speaker for Home, 45W (60W Peak) AC Powered Bluetooth Speaker with Loud Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Built-in Mic, for Home, Office and Gift This speaker seems more designed for more modern music somehow. Maybe it's how current music is mixed. I'm not sure but newer music like Billie Eilish has much more bass than music from the 70s, Led Zeppelin, etc. and even heavy metal from the 80s such as Iron Maiden. The older music, streamed from the same source, comes across flatter with a duller sound. It doesn't sound bad just newer stuff is clearer, has sharper highs and clearer bass.
The speaker is stylish with a nice modern design. There are rubber feet to isolate the unit and keep it from moving. Controls are. . . difficult to use. They're on the back, out of the way. They're dark although somewhat intuitive. Wireless connectivity was easy although the connection drops and reestablishes a few times a week at random times.
Issues with the speaker. I use this in my bedroom. The power/Wireless light is on the front and is a brilliant bright blue. With no other lights in the room this is almost bright enough to read by. I've had to resort to putting a piece of black duct tape over the light so I can sleep at night. The speaker has a narrow band where it sounds good; with the volume low the tone is flat and dull. Crank the volume and something, I think the passive bass radiator, buzzes horribly. Inside that volume window where the sound is good it's pretty darn good but it has it's limits. Not sure if it's my app or the speaker but every, single, time it loses wireless connection for more than a few seconds my volume, bass and treble settings reset back to flat defaults. It's only a mild annoyance but it's there.
text_fidelity_b: ASIMOM Bluetooth Speaker for Home, 45W (60W Peak) AC Powered Bluetooth Speaker with Loud Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Built-in Mic, for Home, Office and Gift

Wiremold Cordmate Cable Management Box, CCBP8-WH,White I have reviewed several similar products and while this could work for some I found the design of this cable management box needs a bit of redesigning.

The point of cable management is to keep your cables looking neat and tidy - this can help achieve that - as long as your plugs are relatively small. While there are four rotating outlets on the ends they are close together and depending on the size of you power adapter plug many will block the plug next to it. I found this was also the case with the outlets located on the top.

This is nearly always an issue with power strips of any sort but when you try to add a cover this becomes even more challenging.

This brings me to the cover design. The side wings expand and must be spread to the maximum width in order to unlock and lift the lid - and even then it’s not easy. This inner cover is thin and not very substantial. Once the other wings cover it that is protected but access is difficult.

Typically I am a big fan of Legrand products and find their designs innovative, helpful and user centric. I cannot say that about this product after testing it for a while.

In real world use I simply have too may power adapter plugs and USB powered devices for this to be a viable solution at my desk. I found it works ok for my entertainment center though I already had my plugs organized there.

In the end, I would recommend one of the more simple box style cord management systems. These allow the greatest flexibility and are definitely far less frustrating to use.
text_fidelity_b: Wiremold Cordmate Cable Management Box, CCBP8-WH,White

ViewTV Digital TV Converter Box for Analog TV - AT-163 OTA DVR, PVR Digital TV Recorder and ATSC Tuner Features A Built in USB Port, HDMI and Coaxial Output, Bright LED Clock and is Easy to Use First I want to say that the first box I received did not work correctly immediately. The box kept failing to maintain recognition that my external drives were in fact present, no matter how many different types I used. There was surely something wrong with the ViewTV. (The ViewTV I received had software version installed from last month.)

I called the ViewTV company and they were really great. The nice tech support guy agreed I had to have something wrong with the unit...and he rushed me out a replacement. The replacement works much better...and interestingly its software version is dated 7 months ago.

I think the ViewTV at $50 is really a great value. (And I was impressed with the customer service the company provided.)

Running the antenna channel scan is relatively fast. The picture quality on my replacement box is stellar. Moving through all the settings menus is very easy and straightforward. Everything is easy to figure out.

When you think about the box's limitations, as pointed out by some very helpful reviews here, you must keep in mind the very reasonable price.

For $50 you get a good over the air box with a good tuner that sends a great picture via HDMI to your TV. You can time shift your viewing, if you plug in a drive to the USB port, and you can record programs to said drive.

For $50 you cannot expect multiple tuners or a great TV Guide. But at least you get to see the very basic guide info the broadcasters send down with their OTA signal. (My two HDTV's on their own do not show the OTA program info, which is very disappointing.)

For cable cutters out there on a budget, this box is definitely something you should consider. It delivers really well exactly what it promises.
text_fidelity_b: ViewTV Digital TV Converter Box for Analog TV - AT-163 OTA DVR, PVR Digital TV Recorder and ATSC Tuner Features A Built in USB Port, HDMI and Coaxial Output, Bright LED Clock and is Easy to Use

It looks and feels cheap when compared to others, with the magnetic mesh filters moving out alignment whenever the case is even slightly moved (these also bent quite easily btw), and 3 of the screws that hold the clear acrylic side lost their thread and were loose ever since.

Mine was pretty loud with the 5 fans I put in to help with temperatures. I knew that heat at some level hurt performance, but I had no clue how much my own rig was being crippled by it until I got a new, different case. I've been able to significantly move up my graphics settings in Witcher 3, Battlefield V, and Shadow of The Tomb Raider, and my framerates are still higher and more stable than they used to be when I was using this case. The fact that it feels more as if I upgraded my gpu after moving on from the Q300L shows how much of a drag the temperatures in this case are to gaming performance (I have a 1070 Ti). I had heard about it from tech youtubers and critic reviews but refused to believe it could be this bad until having another case myself and seeing the difference. There are much better cases out there in terms of airflow, it's not worth having this one reduce the performance of your components so much if you're a gamer

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3 I'm terrible at learning languages. I studied French in junior high, high school and a few years in college, but I still had trouble speaking French fluently. I went to Paris a few times and even dated a French native who criticized every word I attempted, so I gave up. Despite this history of failure, I was curious to see if this Instant Immersion French kit would work for me. The box claims that it is just as good, if not better than Rosetta Stone because they refuse to spend as much on advertising. Hmm. I have a hard time believing that advertising is a main reason why Rosetta Stone is popular. The set comes with 4 CDs and the instructions recommend starting with the Ipod audio CD, though the same sheet of instructions say that it should be used as a supplement to the software. As I sampled each disc, I found that the set is really designed less for a serious French student than for a traveler or someone visiting France on business. There is no attempt to teach grammar or language structure, like present or past tense. The lessons all stress memorization and the ability to recognize and parrot standard phrases, remember a good amount of vocabulary (though not the context to use it). I was disappointed to find that it is structured more like a Berlitz language course. Using flashcards and games to learn language is nothing new, and the Oscar Lake game included is absolutely ancient, as I remember this game from 1998. The only "new" thing about this immersion program is the fact it offers an Ipod and interactive DVD option. The interactive DVD was fun to use though the video is low-tech. Also, the quizzes didn't work that well - I had to click my DVD remote arrow buttons several times before it registered my choice. Did all this it work for me? Did my ability to pronounce words improve? So-so. While I enjoyed playing the games and had fun refreshing my memory using the interactive DVD, the kit offers no real revolutionary way to learn language. It all depends on the student and how motivated you are. In that case, I'd probably do well with Berlitz if I'd only tried harder.
text_fidelity_b: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3

Epson ProSense 347 GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate and Ultra Long Battery Life - Black I've been testing this Epson ProSense watch for the past week. I also have a 2-year-old Garmin Vivoactive HR watch that has most of the same features, but costs half as much. To the compare the two, I've been wearing one watch on each wrist and going on runs and bike rides to see how their readings compare. Both watches have daily step counters that give similar results (today, Garmin says 12044 steps while Epson says 12790 steps). 5% difference is close enough for me.

When I use the GPS exercise mode, the results start showing big differences. On today's run, Garmin recorded 4.02 miles while Epson says 3.9 miles. That's a 3% difference which is close enough for me. Garmin says 529 calories and Epson says 955 calories. Garmin says 535 feet of elevation gain and Epson says 1142 feet. I know Garmin has a barometric altimeter, while Epson is using GPS elevation, which is notoriously inaccurate. Does Epson's terrible elevation data cause a wildly inaccurate calorie count? I could not find any information on Epson's calorie calculation in their documentation, so I really cannot trust it.

Both devices give me heart rate readings with graphs by time or broken out by training zones. The numbers look close enough for my purposes. Both devices also give me maps of my route, which is is nice to have for reviewing later, especially if it is a new route to me.

The Epson is a much larger device (both width and thickness), as shown in the photo. While the Garmin is not especially attractive, at least it is relatively unobtrusive. Epson is big enough to feel clunky on my wrist, especially if I am wearing it all day (to take advantage of the step counter).

Both devices have a smartphone app that syncs your data and also sends notifications to the watch. I'm using this watch with a Google Pixel Android phone. The Garmin app by default uploads your data to the Garmin website. With Epson, you have to upload to a 3rd party website like Strava, which may not be compatible with all the data that your device is collecting.

Notifications work much better with Garmin than Epson. For incoming phone calls, both Garmin and Epson will display the caller ID or contact name so I don't have to pull out my phone to see who is calling. For incoming emails, Garmin displays the sender name and subject line, while Epson just says "you have mail". For text messages, Garmin shows the contact name and message. Epson shows no notification for text messages.

The only advantage (for my use case) that I can find with this Epson watch is the much longer battery life. Garmin claims 1 week of battery life with the GPS off or 13 hours with the GPS on. Epson claims 46 hours of battery life with the GPS on, which I suppose is great for some ultra endurance sports. For me, I never exercise more than 8 hours in a day.
text_fidelity_b: Epson ProSense 347 GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate and Ultra Long Battery Life - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!
text_fidelity_b: Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H Though I received this Acer Chromebook for review, I have another one exactly like it that I bought refurbished about a month ago and have been using it a lot. They are both the same make and model. What I like:

1. The battery life is exceptionally long. I can get a long play list going and it will run all night with nearly a full battery in the morning. I'm using Bluetooth earbuds and I darken the screen so I'm sure that helps to save on battery power.
2. Connects quickly with all my Bluetooth earbuds (and I have several). Only one set of earbuds won't connect and I am still trying to figure that out.
3. Boots up quickly - very short wait time.
4. Screen is nice and big and easy to see.
5. Touchpad works great.
6. Keyboard feels good to use and I'm a very fast typer.
7. It was easy to get it started and on-line right out of the box. It didn't ask me for a billion passwords.

What could be better:
1. Sound is rather weak and really not very good.
2. Screen quality (color, brightness, clarity, etc....) is average
3. Seems to be kind of slow going from site to site....my desktops are much faster.
4. It seems this Acer chromebook doesn't send a Bluetooth signal (weaker) as far as my old Haier chromebook. If I want to listen to something while in bed I have to move the Acer to the bottom of the stairs so the signal will reach. Never had that problem before.

But, for the price of this chrombook (as of this review it's around $179.00) I think it's an excellent buy. It comes with a power cord (of course) but that's it. It uses the Chrome web browser and all I want it for is to check a few sites, write reviews and cruise Youtube. It would be great for college/high school students and anyone who doesn't mind storing their data in the cloud. My main reason for using Chromebooks is that you don't have to buy anti-virus for them since they can't download any data so working off line is not feasible.

It seems to be constructed well and I'm happy with the refurb, but now hubs can use one to surf the web too.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

text_fidelity_a:
Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications My husband put this on one of the farm Polaris CUV's since installation is beyond what I would able to do. He was able to install it on a ranger using the roof system as the mounting position for the speakers. It installed easily enough - basically clamp the speaker to the roof support bars, make sure to use the included rubber strips to get these to clamp securely or you will be remounting these with the rubber strips again once they slide down. Wiring was simple as it all goes to one plug that attaches to the amp. This does mean you will be mounting all 4 speakers. And since the wiring is together in a harness, some thought is required as to where you put the speakers and a good route to where you want the amp installed. The amp install is simple as it basically needs power (12vdc) and not a lot else. It does come with a handy audio input jack so you can use something like an old iPod for audio input. It also has BNC inputs if you have say a radio that you would want to connect to it so there is some flexibility there. The Bluetooth hook up was simple and works well, but again do not hide the amp behind a lot of metal or this may not work to well.

As far as fit and finish, the only thing I can knock this on is the quality of the clamping hardware finish, but being on a rough duty vehicle this is actually okay.

The bottom line is: Overall installation is simple, and the unit is easy to use.
text_fidelity_b: Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, TIMMKOO 4.0" Full Touch Screen Mp3 Mp4 Player with Speaker, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Music Player with FM Radio,Recorder, Ebook,Clock, Browser (White) Ok, first of all, I want to say I LOVE this player much more than others I've used. My kids are not allowed cell phones in school, but they are allowed music players- however most players that aren't smart devices are really janky with buggy/slow UIs and lots of impairments (I tried encoding a video for one and it wouldn't work unless I used a very archaic codec that required a suspicious Chinese desktop app). This, however, actually runs a stripped down version of Android under the hood. This is a GOOD thing! The UI is very polished and smooth thanks to open source mature OS, and features like video playback are much more robust with a wider variety of formats supported and compatible as a result as well!
The hardware is smooth and the menus are intuitive thanks to being familiar with the Android OS already. It's a very cute device!
So why only 3 stars? Well, the listing claims it has a web browser and FM radio. Both of those things are missing on this model. The truth is, I don't need my kids to have that anyway, but it feels weird that the listing advertises features which aren't there. I think I may have gotten a different model than the one advertised.
I considered side-loading a browser apk since it DOES run android, but the truth is this isn't designed for that sort of use and wouldn't make a difference for the purpose of this review. I'd imagine that there are a lot of possible hacks and modifications possible thanks to the operating system inside if someone wanted to tinker.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, TIMMKOO 4.0" Full Touch Screen Mp3 Mp4 Player with Speaker, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Music Player with FM Radio,Recorder, Ebook,Clock, Browser (White)

text_fidelity_a:
ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version IBI - THE SMART PHOTO MANAGER (US Version) makes it super easy to extract, back up, and share photos stored on my mobile devices. Instead of emailing cell phone photos that I want to share among electronic devices (an iPad Air (3rd Gen), a desktop PC, and a Samsung Galaxy cell phone), I can upload the photos to Ibi via a network connection with only a couple of clicks in the Ibi app.

No longer do I have to address an email, select and add the photos, send the email--and then reverse the process on a second device (open the email, download the photos, and save the photos to the device). All that’s necessary is to take the photos, open the Ibi app, choose “import photos”, select the photos, and hit the import button.

The photos are immediately uploaded to Ibi, and I can access them immediately on all of my other devices. There is no need to clutter up email or to consume precious storage space on my mobile devices, when all I want to do is share photos.

Ibi is extremely versatile. It allows you to sort and organize photos, and create Albums. It allows you to authorize certain people to email photos directly to Ibi. It allows you to set up different areas of Ibi for the use of individuals. It allows you to upload its contents to a PC or other even larger storage device by plugging in a USB cable (not included). It even allows you to stream your videos to a television set (using Chromecast or Roku apps).

Ibi is easy to set up, using Bluetooth. My iPad and my Galaxy phone both found the powered on (plugged in) Ibi in less than 30 seconds. Once set up, Ibi communicates via your home network’s Internet access. When your Ibi app is set up, click on Help, and download the complete user manual (a PDF file). The manual is easy to understand, and will enable you to get the most out of your Ibi.

Ibi is a small drive that easily fits on a bookshelf. It uses just one power cord. I really love this Ibi storage drive. It is simplifying my life.

+++++IMPORTANT NOTE: You should NOT choose “automatic backup” in the Ibi app Settings until you understand how the app works. With automatic backup enabled, Ibi will copy all of the photos stored on EACH mobile device, and you will probably get a lot of duplicate photos. For example, if you have been sharing and storing the same photos on an iPad and a cell phone, Ibi will copy the photos from each device. Worse, if you go into Ibi and delete the duplicates, Ibi will keep automatically adding the photos back as long as the photos still exist in storage on the two different devices.

You will probably want to use “automatic backup” when you first set up your Ibi. That way all of your photos will be automatically copied to Ibi to start you off. But you should turn “automatic backup” off before you start deleting duplicate photos. You will never have a problem with duplicate photos if automatic backup is turned off.+++++
text_fidelity_b: ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Let me start, we are a family of dedicated logitech-harmony remote users for the over 7 years. We love the easy of set up and allowing you to out in a large number of electrical devices onto one remote.

So we decided to try this one for our bedroom devices and we were somewhat disappointed with the limitations on this model:

1. when using the harmony software there were a lot of limitations when compared with the 900 (and previous models). The limitations included:
a> couldnt change the order of the activities. ie if you want dvd ahead of music, you would not do that. To over come this: you need to preplan the order at which the devices are set up. In the more expensive models and in previous older models, you could set everything up and then re-order them.

b. once you are in a device: it only offers you four functions on the face, instead of 6 to eight. to overcome this you need to scroll to another page.

c. the device has four hard buttons to operate only four devices. Hence this remote is not useful if you have a decent home theatre. okay for a bedroom with a TV, tivo, dvd and music system.

Typical features of the device: all the button light up in the dark, except for the four device buttons and the help button (so you need to learn where they are on the remote). A good thing about this device (we also have the 900) is that the bottom half of the device have a very similar layout so no learning where the volume, channel button are placed.

The software is similar to other harmony remote, but once you indicate which remote you have: the choices are very limited.

It is worth buying the 900 and above for living room devices; and if you could find the 880, its former model, get it as the functionalities are much better. And yes, the software will support this older model. Buy the 700 if it is only for a couple of applicances. However, if you are a harmony user, you will feel a little frustrated with the limitations of this model.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Like the other two, this is a little larger than initially expected, but it has to be to have all the built-in adapters. There is still no Italy plug or ground conductor, so this is only ideal if you only have an ungrounded device like a computer (again, without ground) and a few USB-chargeable devices like phones and cameras.

This one has a USB-C port, unlike one of my others, but - unlike the one I have that does have USB-C - the total current is more limited. Both adapters with USB-C ports only support 5v output, so they may not charge your device if your device can only accept higher voltage (USB-C has multiple layers of standards, so can be a bit confusing).

I like this adapter when traveling to multiple regions within one trip. Otherwise, I'll just use the cheap adapters which by themselves are smaller. Out of the three I own, I'm not sure which is best; I think it depends on your personal situation. Hopefully I shared enough to help you decide.
